explanation: Some are taller than a person and were quarried on Palau, hundreds of kilometres away. Big stones were rarely moved: everyone simply knew who owned each one.

claims.text: Rai, the traditional money of Yap, are large stone discs, usually with a hole in the centre.
Yapese rai were not whale teeth, feather coils or brass rings.
Some rai stones are taller than a person.
Rai stones were quarried on Palau, hundreds of kilometres from Yap.
Large rai stones were rarely moved; their ownership changed by common agreement.
